item.title: About this demo
item.description:
GraphQL Documentation with Hugo Book#

This is a demo site showcasing GraphQL schema documentation generated by GraphQL-Markdown using the Hugo Book theme.

Getting Started#

  1. Generate GraphQL docs:

    npm run generate

    This creates GraphQL documentation in content/graphql/.

  2. Preview locally:

    npm run dev

    Opens the site at http://localhost:1313.

  3. Build for production:

    npm run build

    Creates static site in public/.

Features#

  • 📖 Clean, book-like documentation theme
  • 🔍 Full-text search across all pages
  • 🌓 Auto dark/light mode switching
  • 📱 Mobile-friendly responsive design
  • ⚡ Lightning-fast static site generation

What’s Inside#

Navigate to the GraphQL section in the sidebar to view the auto-generated schema documentation. All types, queries, mutations, and subscriptions are documented with descriptions and field details.

deprecated#

Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

directive @deprecated(
  reason: String!

item.title: ID
item.description:
ID#

The ID scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as "4") or integer (such as 4) input value will be accepted as an ID.

item.title: projectChanged
item.description:
projectChanged#

Receive an event whenever a project changes in the workspace.

projectChanged(
  projectId: ID
  types: [ProjectEventType!]
): ProjectEvent!

Arguments#

projectChanged.projectId ● ID scalar#

Limit events to a single project.

projectChanged.types ● [ProjectEventType!] list enum#

Limit events to these change kinds.

Type#

ProjectEvent object#

A change delivered to subscribers watching a project.

Example#

subscription WatchProject($projectId: ID, $types: [ProjectEventType!]) {
  projectChanged(projectId: $projectId, types: $types) {
    type
    occurredAt
    project {
      id
      name
      status
    }
    actor {
      name
    }
  }
}

item.title: search
item.description:
search#

Search folders, projects, and users from a single endpoint.

search(
  query: String!
): [SearchResult!]!

Arguments#

search.query ● String! non-null scalar#

Text matched against folder, project, and user names.

Type#

SearchResult union#

A result returned from global workspace search.

Example#

query SearchWorkspace($query: String!) {
  search(query: $query) {
    __typename
    ... on Folder {
      id
      name
    }
    ... on Project {
      id
      name
      status
    }
    ... on User {
      id
      name
      email
    }
  }
}
